paragraphs.text: Explorer context-menu entry that opens a folder as a DSH project, with a switch in DSH settings
# dsh-open-project

> **Current version: 1.4.0** — see Changelog. If you installed an earlier version,
> update: 1.2.0 b

rings the DSH window to the front, and 1.3.x can start the app from a
> non-default install director
y and no longer fails silently.

A DSH plugin for Windows: it adds **用 DeepSeek Harness 打开** ("Open in DeepSeek Harness")
to the Expl

orer folder context menu, and registers the clicked folder as a project in DSH's
sidebar. One switch
in DSH's **Settings → General** adds or removes that menu entry.
It is a two-half DSH plugin:
| Half | File | Role |
| Host | `lib/index.js` | Registers two exact routes on DSH's web server: one that registers a direc

tory as a project, one that reads/toggles the context-menu entry. |
| Client | `client.js` | Renders

one row in the General settings page with a switch that calls the toggle route. |
| Windows helpers
| `cli/` | The registry writer (`context-menu.ps1`), the shared executable lookup (`app-path.ps1`),
and the launcher the context-menu entry actually runs. |
## Requirements

- **Windows 10/11.** The whole feature is an Explorer + `HKCU` registry mechanism.
- **PowerShell —

either version, nothing to install.** Windows PowerShell 5.1 ships with
Windows 10/11 and is enough

on its own: the scripts avoid syntax that only 7 accepts, and they
are saved as UTF-8 with a BOM so

5.1 decodes their non-ASCII default title correctly. When
PowerShell 7 is installed the plugin uses

it instead, because it starts roughly three times
faster. The visible difference is the success noti

fication: 5.1 shows a real Windows toast
(it can project WinRT), while 7 falls back to a tray balloo

n.
- **`wscript.exe`** (ships with Windows) — the menu command runs through it so no console
window

flashes.
- **A DSH profile that composes this plugin** and provides the `webServer` and
`workspaceRe

gistry` services — the ones the DSH desktop application itself uses (its sidebar
project list is bui

lt on the workspace registry). If either service is missing, the plugin
stays pending instead of hal

orkspace registry). If either service is missing, the plugin
stays pending instead of half-mounting.
## What it actually does
Nothing here is more than it looks; this is the exact chain.

**Context-menu click.** The registry command runs `wscript.exe //nologo` with the absolute path
of `

cli/open-project-in-dsh.vbs` and the clicked folder (`%V`) as its argument; that starts
`cli/open-pr
oject-in-dsh.ps1` in a hidden window. That script:
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations

- **It does not change any working directory.** Registering a folder only adds a project
record. A s

ession's working directory is DSH's business, not this plugin's: DSH resolves it
as the project's di

rectory when a session is created from a project, and otherwise as the
host process's own directory

(`process.cwd()`), which is fixed when the application starts.
The plugin never sets or changes a `c

wd`, never retargets the app, and cannot move a session
that is already running. What it does is mak

e the folder *available* as a project; a session
you then start from that project runs in that folde

r because DSH does that, not because the
menu item changed anything.
- **Windows only.** Other platf

orms have no Explorer context menu, no `HKCU`, and no
`wscript.exe`. The host reports `supported: fa

lse` there, and the client row is not rendered
at all — so nothing appears in Settings rather than a

switch that cannot work.
- **PowerShell is started once per action**, so the menu click and each se

ttings toggle pay a
process start-up (about 0.2 s with PowerShell 7, about 0.8 s with 5.1).
- **Cold

start needs the app executable to be discoverable.** `cli/app-path.ps1` checks
`DSH_DESKTOP_APP_EXE

`, then a running instance, then the `dsh://` protocol handler the
installer registers, then the def

ault Electron install locations. The protocol record covers
custom install directories; an installat

ion that registers neither needs
`DSH_DESKTOP_APP_EXE`. Only the *starting* step is affected — regis

tering works with any
running instance.
- **The menu icon is best-effort.** The same lookup decides

the icon. If it finds nothing, the
entry is written without an icon (`Icon` is removed), and the men

u still works.
- **The screenshots date from DSH desktop 0.2.1-rc.2** (see Effect); the row's exact

appearance follows the app's own settings list, so a future release may style it differently.
- **Th

e settings row follows the browser language; the notifications and the menu label do
not.** The row

picks Chinese when `navigator.language` starts with `zh`, English otherwise.
[该节后续省略]
## Permissions and security

- **Registry: `HKCU` only.** No administrator rights are needed, and nothing outside the two
keys ab
ove is read or written. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File cli/context-menu.ps1 -A

ction disable`
removes them completely.
- **The routes live on DSH's own local web server**, which l

istens on loopback
(`127.0.0.1`) — verified on this machine as `127.0.0.1:19387`. The plugin adds tw

o exact
paths; it does not start a server or open a port.
- **`POST /.dsh-open-project`** requires t

he custom header `x-dsh-open-project` (403 without
it), refuses any `Origin` that is not loopback `h

ttp` (403), refuses bodies over 64 KiB
(413), refuses a non-JSON body (400), requires a non-empty `p

ath` string (400), and answers
405 to any method other than `POST`. Another page cannot forge this r

equest: a cross-origin
fetch that adds the header triggers a preflight the route does not answer, an

d a plain
request carries an `Origin` the route rejects.
- **The route accepts no command.** Its onl

y input is one directory path, which it hands to
the workspace registry. That call requires a fully

qualified path that exists and is a
directory; relative paths, drive-relative paths such as `C:work`

, missing paths, and files
are rejected without creating anything. No shell is involved, and nothing

from the request is
interpolated into a command line.
- **`GET/POST /.dsh-open-project/menu`** take

s no free-form input either: a write must be a
boolean, and it selects one of two fixed actions in `

cli/context-menu.ps1`. This route is
called by the DSH settings page itself and therefore does not r

equire the custom header.
- **No network access beyond `127.0.0.1`.** The plugin downloads nothing a

nd executes nothing
that came in over HTTP.
